title: Nighttime Echoes
description: Explore the bridge between your day and night. Map the thoughts that keep you vigilant when the world goes quiet.

questions.text: As I prepare for sleep, my mind's volume usually...

options.text: Turns down naturally.
Becomes a low background hum.
Becomes louder and more insistent.
Shouts over any attempt to relax.

questions.text: Regarding the events of the day, my nighttime mind tends to...

options.text: File them away calmly.
Briefly review them.
Analyze every conversation for potential cringe.
Loop obsessively on mistakes or worries.

questions.text: If I wake up during the night, my immediate internal state is...

options.text: Sleepy and ready to drift back.
Slightly alert but can relax.
Fully awake, with thoughts immediately racing.
In a state of panic or high alert.

insight_cloud.title: The Hour of Vigilance
insight_cloud.text: Waking up at 3 AM and feeling 'wired' is often due to a cortisol spike as your body misinterprets quiet as 'danger'. It's a primal survival reflex, not a character flaw.

questions.text: Physically, when trying to sleep, I notice...

options.text: My muscles feel heavy and relaxed.
Some restlessness in my legs or jaw.
My heart beating noticeably in my chest.
I feel too 'electric' or jittery to stay still.

questions.text: Do you feel a sense of dread as the sun starts to set?

options.text: No, I look forward to night.
Rarely.
Often; I fear the quiet hours.
Always; I avoid the bedroom as long as possible.
